utterances.text: As far as I could understand, you thought that Vlado was a serious man.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: So you concluded on that day that Vlado was in charge in relation to Cicko?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Just because you knew that he was a serious man?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yeah, not only because of that, but that the other guy could not be a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that your assumption?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether Vlado was a commander or not, and this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that's what's important for me. You can also assume these things.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, and I wouldn't venture any further. I don't have any kind of document that Vlado was a commander or that Cicko was a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: So you merely stated your opinion.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the fact that Cicko could not send me from that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Tell us, please, the driver, Cico, Cica -- what's his name?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Cico.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't really see him ask Vlado, you are merely assuming that he asked Vlado about you?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's my assumption again, because we stopped at the Bungalow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but there were other people at the Bungalow?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: No, I saw him. I said hello to him. I'm not quite clear what exactly is it that you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: You don't understand my question?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes. And I would like to clarify certain things with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to see what you heard, what you experienced as far as that conversation is concerned, and I would also like to know what your assumptions are.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: You have understood me?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: When the Prosecutor asked you whether they wore, these gentlemen, Cicko and Vlado, whether they wore any patches, you stated that they only had HVO patches on.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't see any other patches. There may have been other patches as well, but I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, there was nothing else on the basis of which you could come to a conclusion as to the person in charge?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: You're not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us suppose you didn't know either of them; you only saw the way they were dressed.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: This is not on the basis of that that I reached my conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: So how did you reach your conclusions as to the person in charge?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: It was not on the basis of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I would like you to tell me --

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, how -- what kind of conclusions would you make? because there was one person at the trench and there was another person who was far away from the trench.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not the only fact on the basis of which you can make some conclusions as to the person in charge. There may have been someone who was merely visiting there.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, obviously you haven't been in a war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that's why you are here.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: I told you. I told you about what I saw and what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let us try to sum up then. Is it true to say, and would you agree with me, that you concluded that Vlado was in charge because your idea of Vlado is that he was a serious man.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, you cannot really say that, the way -- according to my appearance, one would think that I'm a commander of a corps. You cannot simply base your conclusions on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a collision between questions and answers, and I don't think it's terribly fair to the witness to have his answer being overridden by counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Pavkovic, could you kindly wait a few seconds. Slow down when you speak. Could you also refrain from asking leading questions? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have any further questions. I have received all the answers that I wanted. Thank you. And thank you, Mr. Zaim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Pavkovic. Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: My questions will be somewhat funnier. You were a member of a soccer club.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: What was the name of that soccer club?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: The club changed its name very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's refer to the period of '92-'93?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: There was no soccer at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: So how long did the club last?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, it closed down in '91-'92. I used to play in a village near Travnik. It was a very good club. Do you know anything about that club?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: No, not really. I'm not really interested in soccer. The reason I'm asking the question is because I'm interested in the membership of that football club. Was that a Muslim football club, a Croat football club, or what?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: At the time where I played soccer, I was the only Muslim there. It was at Dolac. I was the captain, and they were all Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Was it a mixed membership?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: It was a mixed membership. Even today, all soccer clubs are mixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm referring to the period of '92-'93?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, people didn't play soccer at that time. There was a war going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, in addition to that soccer club, was there anything else in Vitez, any other kind of cultural organisation in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well -- are you from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: So whatever you had in Croatia, we had in Vitez as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of any folk club, culture club in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: It's the Napredak from Vitez that you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: But it used to be called Slobodan Princip Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: You're right about that. It was called Slobodan Princip Selo. How long did it exist?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: I was not really involved in folk dancing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was not interested in -- I'm not interested in soccer and you're not interested in culture. It's nice to have something on a lighter note in the courtroom because there's been a lot of serious business.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, you've taken it too seriously.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, going back to this subject, how long did this cultural and arts society exist? Do you know how long it was active for?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing more. Thank you. Just one more question, I beg your pardon. Do you know of the brothers Kupreskic in the cultural and arts society?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, you should have asked me in concrete terms. I knew Vlatko. He played the harmonica. He went to school with me. You should have asked in concrete terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not Vlatko's Defence counsel, I'm the Defence counsel for his relations. I'm interested in Zoran and Mirjan.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: I don't know them personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Have you heard anything about them?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, looking at them now, perhaps -- I don't know. Perhaps they don't know me either.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to ask you if you don't know.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes. Don't ask me then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing vital has been lost, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Would you introduce yourself, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I am Defence counsel Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Pleased to meet you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something with regard to the cinema. How many people were in the cinema -- approximately, of course?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I mean the Muslims, when you were taken there.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: In the basement where I was or in the cinema proper as a whole?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, how many people would you say there were there?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: There were quite a lot of us, about 300.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said that your families could bring you something to eat and that entrance was relatively free.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, but my wife was afraid and she came on the third day --

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Well, that's not my point -- my problem.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you said that this was a cinema and that those inside were under the control of the HVO. That's what the Prosecutor asked you.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, we were under this kind of control.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said that you felt safer in the cinema than you would have been had you been outside. That's what you said. I noted this.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: What do you mean by saying "outside"?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: When you were outside the cinema building, had you been in your apartment at home.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's another matter. It is my opinion that I was safer in the cinema rather than in my apartment, and if Prkacin came to kill me -- you see? They all know who Prkacin is. They're laughing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So that means that there were people who were extremists. They were more extreme than the ones who controlled you in the cinema. You were not maltreated, you were not beaten up.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. Somebody at the parking lot wanted to kill me, and you know who lives up above me: Marko with a sniper living up above.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You also mentioned one other thing, and that was that in the cinema, in the building which is where the cinema was located, that there was also the command of the HVO, the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Not where the cinema was but up above the boiler room where I was. Gerin had an office there, Muazem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said that that was why you felt safer.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, because you can't be killed in the basement whereas up above you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, who guarded you, in fact? Did you have guards? Did you see any guards?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, I would go from the basement up above in front of the cinema, and there would be the HVO police. Everybody used to go there because the hotel is there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Have you been to Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So you were guarded by the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Not the HVO army but the police.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, it's the same, the HVO and the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: No, it's not the same.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, not the HVO -- is not army.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you. The HVO and HVO police; isn't that the same for you? For me, it is.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, it's not quite the same, and the army and the police aren't the same either. We know that everybody was in the police. You don't know this very well yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So all the soldiers of the HVO were in the police; is that what you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, I can't explain to you when you weren't a soldier. I don't know what you want to ask me, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I'm asking you who was guarding you. It's quite easy. There are no tricks. I said the police, the HVO police.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Very well. Ah, you can ask questions more slowly. You were going too fast. So you slow down too and I will too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you see any insignia on their uniforms, the people guarding you, or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: The HVO, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes, the HVO.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes. They had the white thing across here and it says "Police." "Sabirna Police." And whenever I would go up, if he was there, if I knew him, then I would be upstairs. If there was somebody I didn't know, I would go down to my basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, whether you know to what unit Miroslav Bralo, nicknamed Cicko, had belonged. You said that you did not know that he was in an HVO uniform on that day; is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Is that what you wrote down?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Will you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know to what unit Miroslav Bralo belonged?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: The HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Just HVO? No other units?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you. In Vitez.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, there were units. There was the HOS, there were the Black Shirts, the Jokers. There was everything there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was there anybody else?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: I don't know. You know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You were there.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In Vitez.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Do you think I have to know everything?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who were the Black Shirts, to your mind? Who were the Black Shirts? The HOS?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Darko -- the thing that Darko was a member of.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: They know better than I know. I don't know everything. I can't know everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: What about the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: I don't know. There were people from Herzegovina and all kinds.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did you know about a unit called the Skorpion?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: No. Where were they?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I'm doing the asking. Tell me, please, what kind of uniforms did you see on that particular day? Was it the police taking you out of the cinema?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: You mean trench-digging? No, it wasn't the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: It wasn't? Who was it?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Just camouflage uniforms, the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How were you able to differentiate between the police and the regular HVO members?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, the police had the white patches and it said "Police" -- some of them, not all of them, of course -- but those who were in the cinema guarding us were policemen, mostly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And the ones that took you away, who were they?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: From Cajdras. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were they HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, not the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Not the army. I keep asking you whether it was the police or the HVO. Would you listen to me?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: I'm listening to you all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who was it? Who took you trench-digging?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: A young man wearing a camouflage uniform took me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Very well. Did he have any insignia apart from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: I didn't see what he had.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You said that when you found yourself at the trenches, when you were taken to dig trenches, that the HVO soldiers who were in the trenches and you who went digging were equally afraid of Cicko; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell us then, please, why you think that the HVO soldiers were afraid of him as well.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: I could see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How could you tell?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, they said so themselves. They said they were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did he threaten them?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did he issue any orders?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Not in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who else was there with you trench-digging?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who was with you except you yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Of the Muslims or the Croats?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The Muslims.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, there were other people too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: How many of them?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: In that particular group, in my group, 15 to 20 of us. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Did Cicko threaten them?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Only when they made the sign of the cross. Cicko didn't go trench-digging with us up there, he remained in the building. He didn't do the digging, I did the digging.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: So the HVO soldiers, that they were afraid you know from their stories, but you saw nothing to illustrate this?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: What should I have seen?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Well, seen him threatening them or something.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Well, he's not going to threaten them in front of me. All I saw was that they were afraid. There were Serbs up at the frontline too, not only the Croats. In the colony, there were Serbs living there and digging -- and were in the HV up at the frontline.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Now, the physician that you mentioned, the doctor you went to see for an examination, this was Dr. Muhamed Mujezinovic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: He was a regular doctor, a full-time doctor at the health centre there?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: How do you mean? In which health centre?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Well, the health centre in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: No, it wasn't a health centre there, it was just a shelter. I was taken to a shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And that was where the other doctor was as well; I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: His name was Bosko. Pasko Pavlic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Was this an improvised centre?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: How do you mean? I don't know what you want to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Had that existed earlier or was it improvised?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: No, they were shops previously. You would go to the basement for shelter. You would make a bed there and somebody would come there, whereas the real health centre was underneath the cinema, below the cinema. Stari Vitez is across the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And Dr. Mujeznovic worked there, did he? What is he by nationality, ethnically?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: You're provoking me. You really are provoking me. You knew very well that he is a Bosniak, a Muslim, and you're asking what ethnic group he belongs to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask you to be respectful.

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, very well. But I would like her to refrain from provoking me and to put the questions to me properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: You are talking to the Trial Chamber. The Trial Chamber does not know who a Croat is and who was a Muslim. So I think that you ought to behave better. Tell us, please, whether Dr. Mujeznovic was arrested in the cinema; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: He could not have been at two places at the same time. If he was up there, he could not have been in the cinema.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac. I wonder, Mr. Smith, whether you would like to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Briefly, I hope, so that we can move on to our next witness? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I will be brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Kablar, you said that you felt safer in the cinema than in your apartment; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Before? Before I left the camp? Because it was safer for me to remain there than to go back to my apartment, yes. Again, this is my personal opinion, that it was better to stay at the cinema hall than to go back to your apartment after the 30th of April because there was this young man who wanted to kill me when I was at the parking lot. So it was not safe for me or my family, my family consists only of females, they could have easily found shelter somewhere else, but for me, being a male, it was not -- it was more dangerous. Maybe I'm not right, but this is my opinion. When I was released from the cinema hall, I didn't even intend to go back to my apartment. I wanted to leave the town of Vitez. It was a very complicated situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: But you were taken trench-digging from the cinema; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned that you felt that because Vlado Santic knew you, that's what assisted in your release from the trench-digging duties. Do you know if any of the other 15 or 20 men that were trench-digging with you were released by Vlado Santic in the same manner that you were?

utterances.speaker: ZAIM KABLAR
utterances.text: Vlado Santic was not at the line where we did the digging, but others were returned afterwards, maybe five or six hours later on. They were all returned to the cinema hall because when I got to the cinema hall, I saw others there. There was this young man who had an injured arm and there were other young men who were not feeling well, so they were all returned five or six hours later. As to who issued orders and who did what, I don't know. Now, I didn't go back there. Had I not been returned, it's very difficult to know whether others would have returned from the line as well because there were no records, as I said, that were kept. We were all usually taken during the night. Cicko did not have any list with people digging trenches. And there was only this young man who left us at the barracks in Kaonik, he only had the number of prisoners that he was supposed to return.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So I think we may release the witness. Mr. Kablar, thank you so much for giving evidence in court. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I'm afraid we will have to stop at 5.00 sharp, but 30 minutes will be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next witness is a protected witness, name and face protection, and will be EE.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: EE. Yes. And is No. 6 on your old list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, Mr. President, while we are waiting for the witness, just to notify the Court and Defence counsel of a slight change in order for tomorrow. After No. 6 on our list, we would then call No. 9 and then, I believe, number 8 and then, I believe, number 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness EE. I am now going to hand you, with the help of the usher --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: -- a slip of paper with your name on it. Please look at it, do not read it out loud, but indicate whether that, in fact, is your name by "Yes" or "No."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 272.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Now, Madam, you have requested that certain protections be granted you by the Tribunal and, in fact, they have been granted so that your name and your face are protected and that therefore you need not fear but you can provide full and complete testimony at the Tribunal. Furthermore, should there be questions that we need to ask you, such as questions regarding your house or your family members that might indicate your identity, then we will request to go into closed session, and if that request is granted by the Tribunal, that would mean that your voice would not leave this room and would not be heard by anyone outside this room, and so that you could then feel confident to provide full and complete testimony about those matters as well. Do you understand what I've said, and do you have any questions at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE
utterances.text: I understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Just to start, could you tell us when you were born and what village you lived in up until 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE
utterances.text: I was born on the 12th of February, 1952 until the 16th of April, 1993 I lived in the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: And without giving us any names, could you tell us who the members or what the composition of your family was in 1993, on April 16th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE
utterances.text: I had a husband, a daughter and a son.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us the ages of your daughter and son in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE
utterances.text: My daughter was 12, about 12 years of age; and my son was 9, nine and a half years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us too what part of the village of Ahmici you lived in, what area or neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS EE
utterances.text: I lived in the lower part of the village below the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, I'm going to request that the witness use the map and demonstrate more specifically the location of her house. I would request that we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 8th day of October, 1998, at 9.30 a.m. 25
